remaining_issues: Historical native GC/worker-startup SIGSEGV and earlier six outside143 results plus one unobserved original outer exit remain unexplained; successful new probes are not causal fixes.
Metadata snapshots are not file locks. An inode can be reused inside a filesystem clock tick, and changes invisible to observed metadata can evade detection; callers must keep inputs immutable.

O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK are used where supported; protecting the leaf does not lock ancestor directories. Regular file reads may still wait for storage I/O; the SDK timeout is not a whole-preflight deadline.

Native probes use unchanged core CPU PPO with NumPy physics; MuJoCo steps are a separate simple XML-model object-lifecycle check, not G1 or SuperMimic training. Policy/Adam checks are two-stage self parity, not cross-SDK numerical equivalence or continuous-RNG resume parity.

The shared-SDK comparison keeps the bootstrap and imported SDK package file paths/hashes identical, but Python builds, compilers, standard libraries and interpreter runtime dependencies differ. First-case maps also resolve libstdc++ through different Conda/system images. It does not establish Python patch-version causality.
Fresh exits, persistent sessions, PPO updates, MuJoCo steps and preflight/hash-race checks have different units.
